questions.question_text:
The process of communication involves ________, encoding, channelizing, decoding and feedback.
(A) reading
(B) ideation
(C) skimming
(D) writing
questions.answer:
(B)
Explanation: Ideation (forming an idea) is the initial step before a message can be encoded.

questions.question_text:
________ is a type of speech delivered without any prior intimation and preparation.
(A) extemporaneous
(B) manuscript
(C) impromptu
(D) memorization
questions.answer:
(C)
Explanation: Impromptu speaking means delivering a speech on the spot without preparation.

questions.question_text:
Study about pitch and articulation in speech is called ________.
(A) Proxemics
(B) Kinesics
(C) Paralinguistic
(D) Psycholinguistics
questions.answer:
(C)
Explanation: Paralinguistics studies vocal cues such as pitch, volume, and articulation.

questions.question_text:
________ is defined as "a groove or notch made by a cutting tool, such as a saw or an axe".
(A) an edge
(B) kerf
(C) hole
(D) slant
questions.answer:
(B)
Explanation: A kerf is the specific technical term for the width or groove of a cut.
questions.chapter: Unit 2 - English: The Language of Science & Technology

questions.question_text:
Choose the appropriate passive voice form of the following sentence:
They will demolish the entire block.
(A) The entire block is being demolished by them
(B) The entire block may be demolished by them
(C) The entire block will have to be demolished by them
(D) The entire block will be demolished by them
questions.answer:
(D)
Explanation: The simple future active verb 'will demolish' converts to the future passive form 'will be demolished'.

questions.question_text:
The usage once in a blue moon is considered to be a ________.
(A) niche
(B) redundancy
(C) cliché
(D) aberration
questions.answer:
(C)
Explanation: The phrase is heavily overused, making it a cliché.

questions.question_text:
Project proposal is a ________.
(A) specially designed report
(B) document that presents a plan of action
(C) report written for a specific purpose
(D) document for granting fund
questions.answer:
(B)
Explanation: A proposal outlines a recommended course or plan of action for approval.

questions.question_text:
Which of these punctuation mark is used between sentences that are grammatically independent?
(A) colon
(B) semicolon
(C) comma
(D) hyphen
questions.answer:
(B)
Explanation: A semicolon appropriately connects two closely related but independent clauses.

questions.question_text:
Flowchart is a pictorial representation of --------.
(A) process description
(B) comparative analysis
(C) trend
(D) opinion survey
questions.answer:
(A)
Explanation: Flowcharts visually map out the sequence of steps in a process.
questions.chapter: Unit 2 - English: The Language of Science & Technology

questions.question_text:
A report is ________.
(A) an official document written for a specific purpose and for a specific audience
(B) a record for common purpose
(C) an arrangement of facts
(D) none of these
questions.answer:
(A)
Explanation: Reports are structured documents targeted at specific audiences for clear objectives.

questions.question_text:
When Carol called last night, I ________ my favourite show.
(A) had been watching
(B) was watching
(C) watched
(D) was watched
questions.answer:
(B)
Explanation: The past continuous tense is required for an action happening at the time of another event.

questions.question_text:
We were late because we ________ some problems. By the time we reached home, Susan ________ for us for more than two hours.
(A) have, was waiting
(B) had, was waiting
(C) had, had been waiting
(D) had, waited
questions.answer:
(C)
Explanation: 'Had' indicates an action before arriving, and 'had been waiting' describes the ongoing action up to that point.

questions.question_text:
The verb form of 'etymology' is ________.
(A) etymologize
(B) etymice
(C) etymological
(D) etymol
questions.answer:
(A)
Explanation: To etymologize means to study or describe the origin of a word.

questions.question_text:
Words that have the same spelling but different meanings with different pronunciations are ________
(A) homonyms
(B) homophones
(C) homographs
(D) cryptonyms
questions.answer:
(C)
Explanation: Homographs share the same spelling but have different meanings and sometimes distinct pronunciations.

questions.question_text:
Choose the correct homonym:
The plane's ----- made my ears pop.
(A) assent
(B) ascent
(C) accent
(D) asent
questions.answer:
(B)
Explanation: Ascent refers to the act of climbing or moving upward.

questions.question_text:
Feasibility report studies the ________ of carrying out a project.
(A) parts
(B) budget
(C) problems
(D) practicability
questions.answer:
(D)
Explanation: A feasibility report assesses whether a proposed project is practical or viable.

questions.question_text:
"Use the freedom judiciously". This is ---------.
(A) instruction
(B) request
(C) rule
(D) recommendation
questions.answer:
(A)
Explanation: The imperative verb 'Use' forms a direct instruction.
questions.chapter: Unit 2 - English: The Language of Science & Technology

questions.question_text:
Choose the correct parallel structure:
Joe likes ________
(A) running, walking, and being active
(B) running, walking and outdoor activities
(C) running, walking, and be active
(D) runs, walking, and be active
questions.answer:
(A)
Explanation: Using the '-ing' gerund form consistently for all items maintains grammatical parallelism.

questions.question_text:
Choose the appropriate word to complete the analogy that is closest to the one given:
BEES: HIVE
(A) Students: Classroom
(B) Church: Devotee
(C) Bears : Den
(D) Teacher: Cabin
questions.answer:
(C)
Explanation: A hive is the natural home of bees, just as a den is the natural home of bears.

questions.question_text:
Convert the following direct speech into indirect speech:
She said, "My mother is cooking food"
(A) She said that her mother was cooking food
(B) She said that her mother is cooking food
(C) She said that my mother was cooking food
(D) She said that my mother is cooking food
questions.answer:
(A)
Explanation: The pronoun 'my' changes to 'her', and present continuous changes to past continuous in reported speech.

questions.question_text:
The zipper differs from the other three fastening devices mentioned in paragraph 1 in which way?
(a) it has been used in many more ways
(b) it is more recent
(c) it can be used in place of the other three
(d) it is usually made from different materials
questions.answer:
(b)
Explanation: The other devices have existed for thousands of years, while the zipper is a more recent invention.

questions.question_text:
The word "prototype" in line 8 is closest in meaning to
(a) device
(b) design
(c) model
(d) original
questions.answer:
(c)
Explanation: A prototype is an early model built to test a concept.

questions.question_text:
What is the author's main point in the second paragraph?
(a) despite being a successful inventor, Judson failed with the clasp-locker
(b) Judson lacked marketing skills
(c) Judson was a poor businessman
(d) Although Judson invented a workable product, it did not appeal to the public
questions.answer:
(d)
Explanation: The passage notes that despite having a working prototype, the public largely ignored it.

questions.question_text:
The word "it" in line 11 refers to
(a) Judson
(b) Clasp-locker
(c) World's Fair
(d) The public
questions.answer:
(b)
Explanation: The sentence says the public largely ignored 'it', referring directly to Judson's invention, the clasp-locker.

questions.question_text:
The word "refinements" in line 12 is closest in meaning to
(a) improvements
(b) changes
(c) promotion
(d) additions
questions.answer:
(a)
Explanation: Refinements involve making slight changes to improve a product.

questions.question_text:
According to the passage, zippers did not really become a success until
(a) they were used in the apparel industry after 1905
(b) in 1913 after being remodeled
(c) the Army used them in World War I
(d) be the late 1920s
questions.answer:
(b)
Explanation: The text explicitly states it was only in 1913, after Gideon Sundbach remodeled it, that the zipper was a success.

questions.question_text:
The word "gear" in line 16 is closest in meaning to
(a) boots
(b) luggage
(c) equipment
(d) tents
questions.answer:
(c)
Explanation: In this military context, 'gear' signifies the equipment carried by troops.

questions.question_text:
The word "embraced" in line 18 is closest in meaning to
(a) welcomed
(b) considered
(c) discarded
(d) promoted
questions.answer:
(a)
Explanation: To embrace a new idea or product means to welcome and adopt it enthusiastically.

questions.question_text:
According to the passage, the zipper got its name
(a) when used in clothing
(b) in 1909
(c) from Judson
(d) because of its sound
questions.answer:
(d)
Explanation: The term was coined as onomatopoeia, meaning it was named after the sound it makes.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following descriptions best describes the author's last comments about Judson?
(a) admire
(b) sad
(c) envy
(d) celebrate
questions.answer:
(b)
Explanation: The author notes 'Regrettably' that Judson died before seeing his invention's massive success, setting a sad or lamenting tone.
